title: Rapid, contamination-less, and efficient environmental DNA filtration system
author: Yoshida, Yamazaki, et al.

The structure of the solenoid pump filtration system is as follows:•The solenoid pump was covered with a heat-conductive adhesive sheet (HF-C1225, Sunhayato corp., Tokyo, Japan) and equipped with a thermostat to prevent overheating (Fig. 1C).•The power switch, thermostat, and solenoid pump were soldered together, and the connections were insulated using heat-shrink tubing and rubber coating (Fig. 1A, B and C).•The power switch was covered with a plastic bag for waterproofing (Fig. 1A).•The male thread (1/8–27NPT) of the male Luer adaptor (Component No.7 in Table 1) was hand-cut to fit an R1/8 screw, as the outlet of the solenoid pump had a GAS 1/8 thread and then connected to the solenoid pump (Fig. 1B).•The hook was attached to the solenoid pump using a beading thread (Fig. 1A and B).•Luer adaptors or hose barb joints were connected to the tubes, and the connections between joints and tubes were tightly secured using an insulation lock (Fig. 1B). These components were assembled around a solenoid pump coupled with a two-way Luer stopcock (Fig. 1B).•A self-made cover was utilized to safeguard the filter cartridge against the potential disassembly of the filter cartridge under pressure (Fig. 1B).

Filtration using this system was proceeded as follows (as shown in Fig. 4):•Disposable laboratory rubber gloves should always be worn during subsequent procedures to prevent contamination. If gloves were contaminated during work, they were immediately replaced.•The system was sterilized by filling and continuously flowing the lines with 2 L of 2% chlorine-based commercial bleach (Kao Co., Tokyo, Japan) through the lines using a solenoid pump for at least 5 min. After sterilization, the lines were thoroughly rinsed with 2 L of pure distilled water (Milli-Q water, Millipore). The sterilized system was stored in a clean plastic bag until use.•A solenoid pump is attached to the CTD frame using a hook, as shown in Fig. 2A, and the plug is connected to a power source.•Before filtration, the outlet of the Niskin bottle was wiped with clean paper to prevent contamination of the working area. The outlet of the Niskin bottle was connected to the inlet of the sterilized tube.•An assembled filter cartridge with a cover was connected to the outlet of the solenoid pump line, and filtration was initiated.•If the buffer tube (as shown in Fig. 1A, No.4) upstream of the filter cartridge had expanded during filtration, a two-way Luer stopcock was employed (Fig. 1B, No.6) to control the flow rate. This step was necessary as the maximum pressure resistance of the tube (270 kPa) is lower than that of the filter cartridge (310 kPa). Therefore, the buffer tube method was used to regulate the filtration pressure.•After filtration, the lines were thoroughly rinsed with pure distilled water or fresh water using a pump to remove seawater, and the system was stored in a clean plastic bag.•The solenoid pump should be handled with caution due to its extremely high temperature during filtration.

steps.title: Assemble solenoid pump system
steps.instruction: Build the solenoid pump filtration apparatus according to the component list and specifications.

substeps.instruction: Cover the solenoid pump (KP1, Cnkalun) with heat‑conductive adhesive sheet HF‑C1225 and attach the thermostat (opening 110 °C, closing 80 °C).
Solder the power switch, thermostat, and pump together; insulate all connections with heat‑shrink tubing and rubber coating.
Cover the power switch with a waterproof plastic bag.
Hand‑cut the male 1/8‑27 NPT thread of Luer adaptor (Component 7) to fit an R1/8 screw and connect it to the pump outlet (GAS 1/8 thread).
Attach the hook to the pump using a beading thread.
Connect Luer adaptors or hose‑barb joints to silicone tubes:
• Silicone tube 1: ID 3.1 mm, OD 6.5 mm, max pressure 270 kPa.
• Silicone tube 2: ID 6 mm, OD 8 mm.
• Silicone tube 3: ID 7 mm, OD 10 mm.
Secure all tube‑joint connections with an insulation lock.
Assemble the tubes and adaptors around the pump together with a two‑way Luer stopcock (Component 6).
Install the self‑made filter cartridge cover to protect the Sterivex filter cartridge (0.45 µm pore, max inlet pressure 310 kPa).
Verify pump specifications: Power AC110–120 V, 35 W; max pressure 1.5 MPa; max flow rate 750 ml min⁻¹.

steps.title: Sterilize solenoid pump lines
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the assembled tubing before any field use.

substeps.instruction: Wear disposable laboratory rubber gloves; replace immediately if contaminated.
Fill the lines with 2 L of 2 % chlorine‑based commercial bleach (Kao) and run the solenoid pump continuously for at least 5 min.
Rinse the lines thoroughly with 2 L of pure distilled (Milli‑Q) water.
Store the sterilized system in a clean plastic bag until use.

steps.title: Attach pump to CTD frame and Niskin bottle
steps.instruction: Connect the sterilized pump assembly to the water source on the research vessel.

substeps.instruction: Hook the solenoid pump to the CTD frame as shown in Fig. 2A.
Plug the pump power cord into an AC power source.
Wipe the outlet of the Niskin bottle with clean paper to avoid contamination.
Connect the Niskin bottle outlet to the inlet of the sterilized tubing.

steps.title: Install filter cartridge and start filtration
steps.instruction: Mount the filter and begin drawing water through the system.

substeps.instruction: Connect the assembled Sterivex filter cartridge (with its protective cover) to the outlet of the solenoid‑pump line.
If silicone tube 1 (buffer tube) expands during filtration, open the two‑way Luer stopcock to reduce flow rate, because its pressure limit (270 kPa) is lower than that of the cartridge (310 kPa).

steps.title: Rinse and store solenoid system
steps.instruction: Clean the apparatus after filtration and keep it ready for the next use.

substeps.instruction: After filtration, rinse all lines with pure distilled or fresh water using the pump to remove seawater.
Store the entire system in a clean plastic bag.
Handle the pump with caution; it reaches very high temperatures during operation.

steps.title: Assemble faucet filtration device
steps.instruction: Construct the 24‑channel filtering device and associated flow lines for deep‑sea water pumping facilities.

substeps.instruction: Use a monomer‑cast nylon disk (diameter 30 cm, thickness 4 cm) as the base.
Drill 11 mm holes for the 24 flow‑line outlets; attach stopped screws (RC1/4‑19) to the exterior of each hole.
Drill 8 mm holes for the flow‑line outlets; hand‑cut male 1/8‑27 NPT threads to fit R1/8 screws and connect male Luer adaptors to these outlets.
Drill an 18 mm inlet hole; attach a one‑touch fitting connection; secure a stopped screw (RC1/2‑14) at the bottom and attach handles.
Assemble a polyvinyl chloride pipe, a pre‑filter (VYS4UUENJ015), and an additional one‑touch fitting as shown in Fig. 3.
Clamp the flowmeter (FD‑H20, KEYENCE) to the outside of the pipe.
Drill an 8 mm hole upstream of the flowmeter; attach a hand‑cut male Luer adaptor and a two‑way Luer stopcock for the Rinko Profiler sensor line.
Connect a detachable flexible nylon tube (ID 11 mm, OD 16 mm) between the filtering device and the pipeline using one‑touch fittings.
Ensure the total length of each flow line (inlet to outlet) is approximately 185 cm and that all 24 channels have identical lengths for equal flow rates.

steps.title: Sterilize faucet system
steps.instruction: Decontaminate the faucet filtration apparatus on site before each filtration run.

substeps.instruction: Wear disposable laboratory rubber gloves; replace if contaminated.
Saturate the entire line network with 6 % chlorine‑based commercial bleach introduced from the inlet; keep the bleach flowing for at least 5 min.
Immediately connect the system to the faucet at the deep‑sea water pumping facility and open the faucet to flush the lines with deep‑sea water for about 5 min, then close the faucet.

steps.title: Connect filter cartridges and begin filtration
steps.instruction: Install the Sterivex cartridges and start water filtration using the faucet system.

substeps.instruction: Attach 24 Sterivex filter cartridges (0.45 µm pore, max inlet pressure 310 kPa) to the outlet of the filtering device.
Confirm that the filtering device is positioned horizontally.
Open the faucet to initiate flow; monitor total water volume with the flowmeter.

steps.title: Post‑filtration cleanup for faucet
steps.instruction: Remove water from the system and store it for future use.

substeps.instruction: Disconnect the detachable flexible nylon tube below the flowmeter.
Blow air through the tube with a dust blower (GSA01Z, Makita) to expel residual water from the filter cartridges.
Remove the filter cartridges from the filtering device.
Rinse all lines thoroughly with pure distilled or fresh water to eliminate seawater.
Store the entire system in a clean plastic bag.
